explanation: A national assembly chose 16-year-old Michael Romanov as tsar in 1613. In March 1917 Nicholas II gave up the throne to his brother, another Michael, who refused it the next day.

claims.text: The Romanov dynasty ruled Russia from 1613 until 1917, when revolution forced Nicholas II to abdicate.
From 1613 to 1917 is more than 300 years.
The Habsburgs ruled Austria, the Hohenzollerns ruled Prussia and Germany, and the Rurikid dynasty ruled Russia only until 1598.
In 1613 a national assembly, the Zemsky Sobor, elected the 16-year-old Michael Romanov as tsar.
In March 1917 Nicholas II abdicated in favour of his brother, Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich, who declined the throne the following day.
